💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.

No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.

Intense, intelligent and highly demanding, the Belgian has already shown himself to be big on the small things which can combine to make a significant difference.

Che Adams discovered this for himself in September, even though an injury prevented him from being part of the fresh man’s first get together in La Manga.

‘I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,’ he revealed.

‘He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT (Kieran Tierney) was out for a walk when he phoned him.

In a recent development, ‘He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that. But it’s good.

Che Adams' appearance against North Macedonia was his first under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Striker Adams says Pocognoli is more intense than his predecessor and is 'with the times'.

John McGinn is within six goals of the scoring record shared by Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law.

‘In the last camp when I was out injured, he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

‘The camps haven’t changed much, but the manager is definitely more intense. I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad.

‘But he’s really bought into it and wants to help us do well.’.

Hang on a minute. A manager who’s more intense than Steve Clarke? You could be forgiven for thinking that’s simply not possible. But Adams feels it is very much the case.

‘With Steve you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well,’ he explained.

‘But he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do.

‘This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game.

According to recent reports, ‘He is with the times, really. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.’.

John McGinn believes it could be as long as 18 months before it all comes up roses. But, in football, you rarely get that long.

Starting in St Gallen tomorrow, the Belgian could do with some green shoots emerging.

‘He’s a few years younger (than Clarke) and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play,’ added Adams.

‘It just takes time to click, but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants.

‘We have been together for a number of years now, so we know each other’s games.

Industry observers note that ‘You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice. We won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

Sources indicate that ‘He stated to us after the game that it’s about the killer moments and we probably didn’t capitalise on them enough. But it was a win and the first one for the gaffer at Hampden.

‘For every manager they need time, but you saw spells there where the movements and patterns of play were very good.

‘It was very vital to get the win and build up the confidence.

‘You’ve also got to keep in context things like that it was Luke Graham’s first start for us, but he had the confidence to play those passes in the build-up.

‘So, you have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.’.

The comfort for Pocognoli throughout a time of transition is that he can still depend on the old stagers who were central to the success under his predecessor.

On the night when Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps, McGinn claimed a double to put himself within six goals of the scoring record jointly held by Dalglish and Denis Law.

Having just turned 32, there is every chance that the Aston Villa captain can soon claim his own slice of history.

‘It’s amazing for John, he’s such a great person and he deserves it,’ stated Adams.

‘Everyone can see what he’s done for club and country, he puts his heart on his sleeve and gives everything.

‘It’s a pleasure to play with him. I really hope he does do it - and I think he will.

‘He’s not going to stop until he does.

‘Everyone is so pleased for him, he’s the best person I’ve met in football. When I came into the squad I didn’t think we’d have people who would achieve these kind of things.

‘I have loved every single minute of it. We have done some great things here.

‘We have been to three major tournaments now, people are making personal achievements as well. But as a team and as a squad it’s about taking that next step now in tournaments.

‘It’s a pleasure to play with these boys. They’re legends of football.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Real Madrid will aim to post a ninth straight win in all competitions when they resume their La Liga campaign at home to Celta Vigo on Saturday night.
  • Jose Mourinho's side have serious momentum heading towards a period which will see them play eight times before the winter break in Spain halts the season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 11:55, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:59.

Real Madrid will aim to post a ninth straight win in all competitions when they resume their La Liga campaign at home to Celta Vigo on Saturday night.

Jose Mourinho's side have serious momentum heading towards a period which will see them play eight times before the winter break in Spain halts the season.

There were serious questions asked of Real Madrid following their defeat to Atletico Madrid before the September/October international break, but the response from Mourinho's side to the loss in the Madrid derby has been seriously impressive.

Indeed, Los Blancos have won each of their last eight games in all competitions, including their last five in the league, which has allowed them to sit firmly in the title hunt.

Real Madrid have a record of 10 wins and two draws from their 12 league matches this season, with 30 points leaving them second in the La Liga table, only three points behind the leaders Barcelona, who had been threatening to run away with it earlier this season.

Los Blancos actually have the joint-best defensive record in La Liga this season with only 10 conceded - the same as both Celta and Atletico Madrid.

Real Madrid will have revenge on their minds in this weekend's contest, having suffered a stunning 2-0 defeat to Celta in the corresponding match at Bernabeu last term.

The victory for Celta at Bernabeu last season proved to be their first win over Real Madrid since January 2017, while it was their first league success against Los Blancos since May 2014, with this fixture dominated by the capital giants throughout history.

Celta have been solid defensively this season but have found it incredibly difficult down the other end of the field, netting only 10 times in 12 league matches, which is among the worst attacking records in the division at this stage of proceedings.

That stated, Claudio Giraldez's side did manage to put five unanswered goals past Salamanca in the first round of the Copa del Rey on November 13.

Celta's last league match ended in a goalless draw with Levante on November 8, and they at the moment sit 11th in the table, boasting a record of two wins, seven draws and three defeats.

The Sky Blues are also playing in the Europa League this season, presently sitting 27th in the overall table, picking up three points from their first four games of the campaign.

Real Madrid form (all competitions):.

Celta Vigo form (all competitions):.

Real Madrid have been boosted by the news that Aurelien Tchouameni and Bernardo Silva are both back in training ahead of this match.

Tchouameni pulled out of the latest France squad with a groin issue, while Bernardo left Portugal duty early due to an injury problem - both are seen as fit for this match at this stage, although it is unlikely that either will be in the starting side.

The returning Vinicius Junior - back from a domestic suspension - is set to feature down the left, with Yan Diomande, Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe potentially also all starting.

However, Rodrygo (knee), Raul Asencio (leg) and Ferland Mendy (hip) are still unavailable for the capital giants.

As for Celta, all of Ilaix Moriba (knee), Manuel Sanchez (hamstring), Alvaro Nunez (groin), Borja Iglesias (calf), Carl Starfelt (hamstring), Miguel Roman (knee) and Jones El-Abdellaoui (knee) are regarded as doubts at this stage of proceedings.

Ferran Jutgla scored twice against Salamanca in the Copa del Rey last time out, but it is expected that Pablo Duran will be given the nod down the middle.

There is also likely to be a position in the side for the experienced Iago Aspas, who has scored five career goals against Real Madrid.

Real Madrid possible starting lineup:.

Courtois; Dumfries, Konate, Huijsen, Cucurella; Valverde, Guler; Diomande, Bellingham, Vinicius; Mbappe.

Celta Vigo possible starting lineup:.

Radu; Rodriguez, Caceres, Alonso; Rueda, Antanon, Burcio, Carreira; Aspas, Duran, Swedberg.

Celta are capable of making this a tricky match for Real Madrid, but we are expecting Mourinho's side to pick up another valuable three points on Saturday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.
  • Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.
  • Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

According to recent reports, lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof.

Millwall manager Alex Neil noted after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Industry observers note that asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

It has been revealed that “I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”.

Recent findings suggest that west Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo remarked: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”.

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”.

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Looks to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

Sources indicate that MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D.

However, the Championship leaders finally turned up in the second half and pulled a goal back through Mohamadou Kanté before Konstantinos Mavropanos equalised with just 10 minutes to go.

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT.

That was only after Marschall gestured that he had been spat at by Castellanos following a melee in the penalty area.

Tierney did, though, brandish a red card when Kanté pulled back Kyrell Lisbie as the substitute robbed him of the ball on the halfway line and ran clean through on goal.

The foul denied Lisbie the chance to hand Millwall their first win over their bitter rivals for 22 years, much to the frustration of fans who had roared them on from first whistle to last.

In a recent development, RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs.

Describing the atmosphere as “absolutely the best by far” since he joined the club almost two years ago, Neil said: “I told the players prior to the game that this game’s a real rarity and, as a player and as a manager, it’s a privilege to be part of it.”.

Millwall: Marschall; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Sturge; Metcalfe (Servais 81), Mazou-Sacko (Cundle 90); Sykes (Baggott 70), Dykes, Neghli; Arconte (Lisbie 81).Booked: Lisbie 90+5.Goals: Taylor 16, Neghli 45+3.Subs not used: Batth, Crocombe, Doughty, Issoufou, Kelly.West Ham United: Hermansen; Walker-Peters (Kanté 46), Mavropanos, Kilman, Morato; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa (Austbo 68), Solomon; Piroe (Pablo 46), Castellanos (Orford 90).Booked: Morato 40, Pablo 83, Kilman 86, Mavropanos 90+5.Sent off: Kanté 89.Goals: Kanté 74, Mavropanos 80.Subs not used: Ajala, Austbo, Golambeckis, Herrick, Magassa, Scarles.Referee: Paul Tierney.

Industry observers note that 🗣️ 'We were able to bounce back, but we need to look at the things we have not done so well'Nuno Espirito Santo reflects on West Ham's performance after the Hammers fought back from 2-0 down to draw with Millwall. pic.twitter.com/NM1wQVcN0o.

In a recent development, asked by Sky Sports for his view on the “spitting” incident, Alex Neil mentioned: “Fil [Marschall] was saying to the referee throughout the game when that happened at that point... Obviously I’m so far away it’s hard for me to see what happened, but I wouldn’t presume that Fil would say that without cause.

“I’m sure the referee and authorities who need to deal with it will look at it and, if it warrants it, it needs dealt with and then I’m sure they will.”.

In a recent development, "It's one of the best atmospheres I've ever played in..I got shivers walking out"Millwall's Caleb Taylor speaks to Aaron Paul following today's 2-2 draw with West Ham. pic.twitter.com/yFoRuxooe6.

Lisbie darts to the by-line but his cutback does not make it through the thicket of limbs and West Ham clear their lines.

A thunderous chant of “Milllllllll” echoes around the ground as the home fans spur their charges on.

In an attempt to get his foot on the ball, Engels has often peeled out to the right-back position, but a wild, desperate cross-field ball that goes straight to Osei-Tutu sums up West Ham’s half aptly.

A wild challenge from Metcalfe on Cooper earns West Ham a free-kick and its then Sykes’ turn to land a late tackle, this time in the right channel. The subsequent delivery finds Castellanos but he cannot direct the ball goalwards.

Recent findings suggest that west Ham’s strength comes from the fluidity of their front four, but Nuno’s creators have not been able to access them. So effective has Millwall’s back-line coverage been that West Ham have only managed low-quality final-third entries.

Arconte appears to be through but Kilman does well to recover and Dykes’ subsequent shot is charged down.

Sources indicate that west Ham are not learning their lessons and Sturge almost pulls off a similar pass in behind for Arconte, but the linesman raises his flag on this occasion. Replays show that it was really tight.

Sources indicate that millwall are going man-to-man as West Ham try to build and the visitors are struggling to get out. Sturge works infield from his starting perch on the left and almost threads a through-ball in behind for Arconte to gallop on to but Kilman does well to stick in a boot.

West Ham are desperately trying to calm this game down, but the Millwall fans are making that quite the challenge. The visitors string a series of passes together before Bowen strays offside.

Millwall then burst forward, Arconte this time popping up in a dangerous position on the right but Metcalfe fires over having picked off a loose Hammers pass out from the back.

Another Dykes throw-in sparks panic in West Ham’s box. Osei-Tutu’s back-post header appears to take a deflection off Walker-Peters, but the referee awards a goal-kick.

Industry observers note that this rivalry was forged in different circumstances from most derby confrontations. There is none of the religious divide of Celtic and Rangers, or the politics of Barcelona against Real Madrid, or the spat over title-winning superiority of Manchester United and Liverpool. This is a tale of proximity, an internecine feud.

“There’s no politics, no nationality, nothing like that,” says Nick Hart, who hosts the weekly podcast Achtung! Millwall. “We’re very similar people, from the same backgrounds, same communities. But it’s in the Millwall supporter’s DNA for West Ham to be the ultimate rivals. Nobody else comes into the equation. You’re brought up on this stuff. It’s your history.”.

Sources indicate that though possibly more recent history than might be suggested by the two clubs’ early foundations. The hostility that West Ham will face at the Den is no more about dockland rivalry, north-south London disputes or strike-breaking than the animosity when Manchester United visit Anfield is caused by the building of the Manchester Ship Canal.

“It really is about the hooligan era,” states a podcaster who uses the pseudonym Former West Ham Employee on the West Ham Way podcast. “The two clubs had notorious fanbases. And they grated. It came about through vying to be the No 1, battling to see who had the hardest mob. Whenever we’ve played – or even been in close proximity – things have happened.”.

Jake Cooper on making the 500th appearance of his career against West Ham today! 👏Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/lTzXOwXhxd.

Sources indicate that there have only been 18 meetings between these fierce rivals since the Second World War, but absence has certainly not made the heart grow fonder. Here are some of the feud’s most notable flashpoints.

Sources indicate that at the 1972 testimonial in honour of Harry Cripps – the renowned Millwall hard man – police horses were sent on to the pitch after West Ham supporters entered the home section at The Den. Fighting spilt over into the streets surrounding the ground.

An even bleaker turn came in 1976, when Millwall fan Ian Pratt died in a skirmish with West Ham fans at New Cross station that led to his fall under a train.

Leaflets were later handed out in the Den’s Cold Blow Lane end with a grainy picture of Pratt and a declaration in capital letters: “A West Ham fan must die next week to avenge him.”.

Millwall plundered four goals on Mothering Sunday in 2004 as Tim Cahill’s double helped them to a 4-1 victory over West Ham at the Den in an incident-filled derby.

Industry observers note that the hosts missed a penalty and had another saved by Stephen Bywater, who was later sent off. Violence followed in the stands and the match was named “The Mothers’ Day Massacre”.

Mother's Day Massacre ⏮️A 4-1 victory over The Hammers back in 2004. pic.twitter.com/TLi7xkcVJG.

A hundred West Ham and Millwall supporters clashed during a screening of England’s 2006 World Cup match against Paraguay in Canada Square, which led to 16 injuries and one hospitalisation.

The clubs’ League Cup meeting in 2009 at Upton Park was listed as Category Five by police, the most serious risk of violence, and resulted in a Millwall supporter being stabbed in Priory Road, near the ground.

The Metropolitan Police said that “planned” scuffles, which involved more than 100 fans, appeared to have been caused by fans without tickets to the game.

Recent findings suggest that just spotted one Millwall fan outside the ground in blue boxing gloves. He is also wearing what appear to be slippers, so not sure what that means….

Nuno Espirito Santo has only been through the door at West Ham for a matter of months, but he insisted he is fully aware of the significance of today’s fixture.

Recent findings suggest that when asked about his perception of the rivalry, Nuno said: “Since the fixture list came out, this date has been [key], for both of the clubs. It’s special, special game. We look forward to go and compete against a good team.

“It’s a different game from all of the other games, it’s a special game, the atmosphere will be different… Steve [Potts, first-team coach and former West Ham player] has been involved in many of these games, he’s constantly speaking about how special it is for West Ham fans, so we have a lot of information and we are fully aware of the importance of the game.

Sources indicate that on potential unrest between fans and the significant police presence, Nuno added: “What we want most is that everything goes well, both fans supporting their teams and no conflict. We have people inside the club who are taking care of that. We have to focus on our tasks.”.

The gaffer on tomorrow's fixture ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/6NG6t4t4Fn.

#westham on the way to #millwall via #london bridge #whufc #coyi pic.twitter.com/HrWgJ6UtJY.

In a recent development, riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

The game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

According to recent reports, the Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

Alex Neil switches out goalkeeper Max Crocombe for Filip Marschall and names the returning Mathis Servais, Kyrell Lisbie and Alfie Doughty on the bench.

Alex Neil names his Lions XI 👊 pic.twitter.com/MP0N9wMatG.

Just the one change from the league leaders’ last league match as Kyle Walker-Peters comes in for the injured Joel Veltman.

Today's teamsheet 📋 pic.twitter.com/EmrxYRhsPd.

"We have to quiet them down" 🤫West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen is expecting a hostile atmosphere at The Den today 🗣️Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/9tp2225Rq8.

The Metropolitan Police will have 400 officers on the streets of east London for this match – about four times the norm for a Championship fixture – and it has enforced a Section 35 dispersal order in the area highlighted on the map below.

A Section 35 order authorises a Police Constable and a Police Community Support Officer in uniform to “exclude a person from an area for a period of up to 48 hours with an Inspector’s authority”.

It has been revealed that good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the highly anticipated Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United as the two clubs meet officially for the 100th time. This fixture has not been staged since 2012, and the intervening 14 years have done little to temper the ill-feeling between their passionate supporters, who will be anxious to claim bragging rights over their Dockers Derby rivals. The Metropolitan Police have placed a Section 35 dispersal order in the area surrounding The Den and will deploy 400 officers on the streets of east London.

It has been revealed that acrimony between the two clubs has existed since the late 19th century when Millwall Athletic, originally Rovers, battled it out against Thames Ironworks, later renamed West Ham at the Athletic and Memorial Grounds. Sixty of the two clubs’ 99 meetings came between 1899 and 1915, and while they played just seven times between 1946 and 1987, the irregularity of the game only added to its mystique, which has often spilt over into the ugly.

Both head coaches spoke at length about the significance of today’s match, with Alex Neil, in the Millwall dugout, describing it as an encounter that means “absolutely everything” but imploring his players to keep “cool heads”. His counterpart Nuno Espírito Santo revealed that he had been well advised about the game’s importance by Steve Potts, his first-team coach and former West Ham player.

Industry observers note that since the club’s last meeting in 2012, West Ham have ascended into the Premier League, moved into the London Stadium and won the Uefa Conference League, only falling back into England’s second tier last summer where Millwall have remained for all but two seasons. The Lions brushed maddeningly close to promotion in their last campaign as they pushed for an automatic spot until the very last weekend of the regular season before falling to Hull City in the play-off semi-finals.

Much of the pre-match talk will centre on the clubs’ long-standing rivalry, but beneath the bile and belligerence is an intriguing football match between two sides. Millwall are missing 11 first-team players and face the daunting task of stopping a West Ham side who have found their feet in the Championship, scoring 16 goals in their last four league matches.

Geoffrey Moncada, today, has given a bit of insight into how long AC Milan were trying to sign Alphadjo Cisse.

Industry observers note that when Milan signed Cisse, there was a bit of a mixed reaction. Although he was seen as a talent for the future, the money could’ve been spent on a first-team acquisition, with the squad lacking in certain areas.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Now, though, everyone would be glad that the decision was made to sign the young Italian. To say he’s exploded this season would be an understatement and he’s perhaps the biggest gem at the club right now.

Speaking to Calcio e Pepe, as Francesco Nasato relayed on X, Moncada went through the process of the Rossoneri’s scouting of Cisse.

Recent findings suggest that “We had a scout who worked near Verona and he immediately pointed out this boy to us, Alphadjo Cisse, who played for the Under-17s and then for the Primavera, and then for the Under-20s. So we went to see him and he was very interesting.

“Two or three years ago, we launched Milan Futuro. Our idea was to sign him for that team a year earlier, but we couldn’t reach an agreement with Hellas Verona. They wanted to keep him and decided to send him on loan to Serie B.

“We followed him very closely in Serie B, too, and he literally exploded there in the first six months. We told ourselves he’d made such a good transition from the Primavera and Verona’s bench to Serie B that we needed to make a move.

Sources indicate that “It was winter and we had to hurry. If he had gone to PSV and you had wanted to buy him later, perhaps after playing in the Champions League, the price would have risen to €30 or €40 million. Sometimes you have to speed things up a bit.”.

Considering the club had followed him since he was in the Under-17s, it’s a good thing they eventually managed to sign him, especially with the way he’s started at San Siro.

Lincoln City play host to Wrexham on Saturday afternoon with just three points separating the teams in the Championship table.

While Lincoln are in 21st position in the standings, Wrexham's recent upturn in form has moved them into 15th spot.

If Lincoln managers Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw had been offered the chance to sit five points clear of the relegation zone at this stage of the season, they would have taken it.

However, three successive defeats before the November international break have left the pair with much to ponder.

Although losing 3-1 at home to Birmingham City was not necessarily a surprise, Lincoln then succumbed to a 1-0 defeat to struggling Watford.

The Imps then conceded an 80th-minute goal to lose 2-1 at Queens Park Rangers in their most recent fixture.

Industry observers note that cohen's and Shaw's priority will be to improve Lincoln's home form. Despite a 4-1 victory over Burnley on October 24, that remains their only win at the ProAmpac Stadium in this season's Championship.

As far as Wrexham are concerned, Phil Parkinson found himself fighting for his job prior to the international break.

Nevertheless, four points from home fixtures against Middlesbrough and Wolverhampton Wanderers have at least bought the long-serving boss some time.

While Wrexham remain six points behind the playoff spots, there is at least a feeling of optimism on the back of encouraging results versus the second and fourth-placed teams in the division.

That remarked, the Welsh outfit have gone five matches without recording a win on their travels, while they have netted just five times across seven away fixtures.

Lincoln City Championship form:.

Either Ivan Varfolomeev or Tom Bayliss are expected to replace Lincoln midfielder Conor McGrandles, who is serving a one-match ban.

While Ben House is available again after suspension, the attacker may only be named on the substitutes' bench.

Rob Street could come back into the team to replace Mikkel Ladefoged, depending on whether Cohen and Shaw go with a 4-2-3-1 or 4-4-2 formation.

If Kieffer Moore is ruled out of this fixture through injury, Bailey Cadamarteri may be handed a rare start in attack.

With Issa Kabore also a fitness doubt, Danny Imray is on standby to deputise at right wing-back.

Josh Windass and Nathan Broadhead are again expected to miss out through injury, while Sam Smith is a long-term absentee.

Lincoln City possible starting lineup:.

Wickens; Oyegoke, Elerewe, Bradley, Reach; Hackett, Konak, Varfolomeev, Jefferies; Draper, Ladefoged.

Wrexham possible starting lineup:.

Patterson; Worrall, Cleworth, Doyle; Kabore, Dobson, Rathbone, Whiteman, Ekomie; O'Brien; Cadamarteri.

For different reasons, this has the potential to be an crucial fixture in the context of their respective seasons. Although home advantage and a two-week break could benefit Lincoln, Wrexham may edge this contest, with Parkinson likely tempted to push for all three points in a tight game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.

Sebastien Pocognoli has conceded that he doesn’t have 18 months to demonstrate that Scotland are on the right track under him.

Appointed Steve Clarke’s successor in the summer, the Belgian’s attempts to bring in fresh faces and a upcoming style of play has produced mixed results in his opening five Nations League games.

Following Friday’s win over North Macedonia, John McGinn warned the Tartan Army that it could take as long as 18 months for everything to click into place.

But ahead of the final group match in St Gallen tomorrow evening, the manager acknowledged it’s incumbent on him to accelerate that time frame.

Asked if he felt he had to deliver sooner, he remarked: ‘Yeah, for sure, but we’re only talking about 18 months because John said that. He could have said 15 months. I don’t know. But, for sure, it needs to be quicker.

In a recent development, ‘In 18 months, it will be the time of the Euros and that is what he meant. We have to go there and be prepared for this in 18 months’ time.

Sebastien Pocognoli  notes his Scotland team need to show progress 'game after game'.

‘For sure, game after game, we need to see improvement.

‘Some new faces will come back in March. So, step by step we will have more ideas and in one month’s time a lot can change also.’.

McGinn also said that the players were fully behind the manager, reiterating the point previously made by Andy Robertson and Scott McTominay.

‘I can tell you that in the time we have had together the players have been doing well in terms of replicating what I ask them to do,’ the manager stressed.

‘They know that and that’s the most important part.

In a recent development, ‘They buy in. They like it. I think they enjoy it too. You can see when players don’t enjoy it.

‘For sure, when you win it’s more enjoyable, but it would be very bad if they weren’t enjoying it and we were also not winning games.

‘So, right now I think we are working well. We give special attention to the collective.

According to recent reports, ‘In all the camps, I am very clear about what I expect on the pitch. The players wanted this when I arrived. They wanted clarity. And I think that’s what I have tried to bring.’.

To claim second place in the group, Scotland need to defeat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t win in North Macedonia.

That outcome would ensure that Pocognoli’s men would be a pot two side in next month’s Euro 2028 draw.

Asked what it would take to pull off what would be a stunning win in St Gallen, the manager noted: ‘Let’s be brave, but be intelligent.

‘It’s about mentality. They (Switzerland) are a very good team, so we need to be smart. Sometimes they will go through our lines with a low block or a high block as they have the quality.

‘We will try to be intense and strong in the duel because I think that’s the first piece to have a good game.’.

Pocognoli’s side were booed off at half-time on Friday with criticism of the performance persisting despite them going on to win the game.

But the manager claims he’s oblivious to wider concerns about the performances to date, saying: ‘No, I’m not aware of this. That’s why I was surprised (at the question).

John McGinn suggested that it could take 18 months for Scotland to click under Pocognoli.

In a recent development, ‘Yes, there were some boos at half-time. I think that’s part of it, it’s been like this for years.

‘I know we are colleagues, but I’m not reading the press.

Sources indicate that ‘So, I’m not aware of the criticism. I just want to make the supporters happy.

‘If they aren’t yet happy, we will try to do better.

It has been revealed that ‘There’s pressure in all the jobs with a club. It can be external, it can be internal. It is part of the job.

It has been revealed that ‘I’m very self-critical about myself. So, that’s the first thing. Try to be stable when we win, when we lose.

Industry observers note that ‘I’m always thinking what we can do better. If there’s some criticism, that’s fine.

‘But there there were also a lot of positives after the North Macedonia game.

‘I was the first one to say calm down as we need to see more.’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 11:56, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:47.
  • Aiming to avoid back-to-back league defeats, Plymouth Argyle welcome Peterborough United to Home Park for a League One clash on Saturday afternoon.
  • The Pilgrims were dispatched at the base of title-chasing Sheffield Wednesday last weekend, whereas Posh are in the midst of an on-field crisis despite a recent managerial change.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 11:56, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:47.

Aiming to avoid back-to-back league defeats, Plymouth Argyle welcome Peterborough United to Home Park for a League One clash on Saturday afternoon.

The Pilgrims were dispatched at the base of title-chasing Sheffield Wednesday last weekend, whereas Posh are in the midst of an on-field crisis despite a recent managerial change.

After missing out on the League One playoffs on the final day of last season, Plymouth Argyle are desperate to crash the top-six conversation this time around; however, a recent result certainly brought supporters back down to Earth.

The Pilgrims were enjoying a four-game unbeaten run (W3 D1) across all competitions before a harrowing afternoon at Hillsborough last weekend, when goals from Billy Mitchell, Davis Keillor-Dunn and Di'Shon Bernard secured a comfortable 3-0 success for Sheffield Wednesday.

Now looking to dodge consecutive defeats, Tom Cleverley's side are at the moment occupying sixth position in the League One table, just six points behind pacesetters Huddersfield Town and Stockport County in first and second respectively.

The Devonshire outfit are unbeaten across their past three home matches against Reading (0-0), Alvechurch (4-0) and Swindon Town (2-1) in all competitions; however, Plymouth have actually collected more points away from Home Park this season.

The summer departure of fans' favourite Lorent Tolaj to Bristol City has increased the goalscoring burden on Canadian marksman Aribim Pepple, who has netted on five occasions in League One during 2026-27.

In April 2025, Peterborough United experienced one of the proudest days in their humble history, beating a record-breaking Birmingham City side at Wembley Stadium to earn consecutive EFL Trophy crowns.

Eighteen months on, the Posh are enduring a severe fall from grace, with club chairman Darragh MacAnthony admitting that his side are not performing anywhere near the levels expected at the moment.

The form table strongly supports MacAnthony's argument, with Peterborough losing each of their past four competitive matches without finding the net, suffering embarrassing losses to Reading (0-5) and Luton Town (0-3) since the start of November.

Winning just two of his opening nine games in charge, head coach Robbie Savage has failed to turn the tide at Weston Homes Stadium as of yet, with Saturday's visitors sitting in 22nd spot in the League One rankings.

Looking on the positive side, an unexpected victory in Devon could take Posh out of the relegation zone this weekend, with Peterborough victorious on their most recent trip to Plymouth in September 2025.

Plymouth will be without the services of defender Alex Mitchell, who remains sidelined due to an unspecified muscular injury.

The absence of the 25-year-old adds to the Pilgrims' backline complications, with Spaniard Julio Pleguezuelo unavailable because of a calf problem.

As a result, Wes Harding, Mathias Ross and Alex Hatridge are the hosts' only centre-back options for Saturday's clash.

Tom O'Connor injury-plagued 2026 continued earlier this week, with Peterborough's Irish defender picking up another hamstring injury in the loss at Luton.

The 27-year-old is set to be sidelined for up to six weeks, joining youngster Lucca Mendonca in the medical room.

Plymouth Argyle possible starting lineup:.

Cooper; Harding, Ross, Hartridge; Curtis, Boateng, White, MacKenzie; Amaechi, Ibrahim; Evans.

Peterborough United possible starting lineup:.

Bass; Dornelly, Hughes, Feeney, Mills; Kelly, Garbett; Shofowoke, Williams, Khela; Leonard.

After the disappointment of defeat by Sheffield Wednesday last weekend, Plymouth are now presented with a great opportunity to respond at Home Park.

In the midst of crises on the pitch and in the medical room, Peterborough are hurtling towards a fifth consecutive loss in all competitions.

#3143. Latest Update: Sergio Navarro’s style and the key individuals: Milan Futuro tactical analysis

Latest Update: Sergio Navarro’s style and the key individuals: Milan Futuro tactical analysis

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (967 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Milan Futuro decided to go in a latest direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?
  • Recent findings suggest that milan launched the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Milan Futuro decided to go in a latest direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Recent findings suggest that milan launched the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

According to recent reports, with promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

Recent findings suggest that milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

According to recent reports, asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

It has been revealed that this also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

Similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

In a recent development, milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

Milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most notable aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

Industry observers note that rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

One of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

It has been revealed that perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

In a recent development, at times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 12:05, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 12:06.

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho could select an extremely attacking team in Saturday's La Liga contest with Celta Vigo.

Los Blancos have been boosted by the news that Aurelien Tchouameni and Bernardo Silva are both back in training ahead of this match.

Tchouameni and Bernardo had been serious doubts due to injuries sustained on international duty with France and Portugal respectively, but the pair are set to be in the squad.

That said, it is unlikely that either will be named in the starting side.

Arda Guler could therefore drop back into a midfield position alongside Federico Valverde, with the returning Vinicius Junior set to start down the left; Yan Diomande, Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe should also be in the XI.

Vinicius has now served his four-match domestic suspension and is available for selection.

However, Rodrygo (knee), Raul Asencio (leg) and Ferland Mendy (hip) are still out.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is an option to start at right-back, but Denzel Dumfries could ultimately be given the nod in that area of the field.

Real Madrid possible starting lineup:.

Courtois; Dumfries, Konate, Huijsen, Cucurella; Valverde, Guler; Diomande, Bellingham, Vinicius; Mbappe.

QPR set to welcome key player back for Millwall clash – he must come straight into the starting XI: Opinion

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (557 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, QPR return to action after the international break with a short trip to Millwall on Saturday.
  • Julien Stephan has had to get by without some key players too.
  • Industry observers note that however, ahead of the Millwall tie, Stephan has confirmed Madsen is fit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, QPR return to action after the international break with a short trip to Millwall on Saturday. The Hoops have had a fine season to date with only three losses in their 15 Championship games, leaving them 8th in the table and just inside the play-off spots.

Julien Stephan has had to get by without some key players too. Among those sidelined in the early stages of the campaign has been Nicolas Madsen, who won the club’s Player of the Season award last term and impressed early on in 2026/27.

Industry observers note that however, ahead of the Millwall tie, Stephan has confirmed Madsen is fit. He was tentative when asked whether the Dane would be fit to start, but if he’s good to go, he should come straight into the QPR midfield.

Madsen’s QPR redemption has been a joy to watch. He had a tough first season after arriving in the summer of 2024 but grew into a crucial role over the 2025/26 campaign, providing a physical presence in the middle with box-to-box threat and good passing.

He chipped in with three goals and six assists last season and had managed two goals and an assist in his last two matches before being cast to the sidelines in October.

It has been revealed that jonathan Varane has stepped in to partner Glen Kamara in the middle in Madsen’s absence. The Frenchman has done a decent job and his own physicality makes him a good ball-winner, but he lacks the Danish ace’s attacking quality and creativity.

Madsen is someone who can truly contribute in all areas of his midfield game. Alongside his nine goal contributions last term, he completed 1,165 passes with 56 chances created and won 63.4% of his duels with 167 defensive contributions. 155 recoveries highlight the ground he covers and his work rate across 90 minutes as well (stats via FotMob).

Industry observers note that with Madsen returning, Stephan can return to his favoured midfield partnership of the 26-year-old and summer loan signing Kamara. The Finn has been among QPR’s best players this season and will deservedly keep his spot despite Madsen’s return.

Kamara is an intelligent player with strong technical ability, while Madsen’s power sees him play the role of a duel winner alongside his progressive abilities on the ball. Ronnie Edwards helps on this front when stepping into the midfield, and the attacking midfielder is usually entrusted with more ball-carrying.

Recent findings suggest that the attacking midfield berth is up for grabs with both Ilias Chair and Karamoko Dembele fit to compete for the place once more. However, behind them, QPR will be happy to return to their strongest partnership of Madsen and Kamara.

By Darren Plant | 19 Nov 2026 12:07.

Wolverhampton Wanderers play host to Charlton Athletic on Saturday afternoon looking for the win that would keep the club in contention for top spot in the Championship table.

At a time when the West Midlands outfit sit in fourth place, Charlton's much-needed victory before the international break has moved them into 17th position.

Although some Wolves fans were disappointed with a 1-1 draw at Wrexham before the two-week break, Cesar Peixoto is right now doing an excellent job at Molineux.

Fourteen points have been collected from Wolves' last six matches to keep them one point adrift of leaders Birmingham City.

Furthermore, Wolves have not conceded more than one goal in any of those fixtures, while four points were accumulated from away contests at Bristol City and Wrexham before the international break.

Wolves now have 14 points from eight away games, the second-best record in the division, but they have only scored one goal in four of their most recent five matches at Molineux.

That will be a cause for concern for Peixoto, whose could still potentially move into first place this weekend if results go their way.

Meanwhile, Nathan Jones effectively kept himself in a job at Charlton with victory in their most recent fixture.

The 2-1 win at home to Sheffield United ended a run of 11 matches without success in the Championship, a run stretching back to August 29.

Charlton sit seven points adrift of the playoffs and seven points above the relegation zone courtesy of their win over the Blades.

Despite the London side registering just one away success in seven such fixtures this campaign, that solitary triumph came at relegated Premier League team West Ham United.

Kieran Trippier, Yerson Mosquera and Hugo Bueno could all be recalled to the Wolves defence.

With Fer Lopez and Jean-Ricner Bellegarde both missing international duty due to minor injuries, they are doubts for this fixture.

As Jordan James remains sidelined with a hamstring injury, Tommy Doyle is an option in central midfield, with Marshall Munetsi potentially being used further forward.

Matty Godden is expected to replace Charlie Kelman in the Charlton attack, reward for his decisive goal as a substitute versus Sheffield United.

Oliver Skipp and Harvey Knibbs will also come into contention for recalls, but the remainder of the starting XI could stay the same.

Wolverhampton Wanderers possible starting lineup:.

Sa; Trippier, Mosquera, Krejci, Bueno; Andre, Doyle; R Gomes Munetsi, Mane; Armstrong.

Mannion; McNamara, Bindon, Koumetio, Bell; Coventry; Alli, Rankin-Costello, Knibbs, Campbell; Godden.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been a positive international break for Diego Moreira, who continued his excellent form from club football.

Recent findings suggest that as La Gazzetta dello Sport write this morning, Ruben Amorim will welcome Moreira back to Milanello soon. The winger has become a regular starter and producing goals and assists, but the Portuguese coach knows the pitfalls of the match against Frosinone all too well.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Therefore, starting Thursday – when the squad will be fully back together after the day off tomorrow – everyone’s minds will be focused solely on the new busy schedule awaiting the Rossoneri until Christmas. More specifically, seven matches from Sunday until December 19th.

In a recent development, immediately after the last international break, the Rossoneri drew away to Sassuolo, a result that certainly wasn’t greeted with a smile. The goal is to avoid repeating that misstep against Alvini’s team, and Moreira will be key to that.

Despite his 22 years of age and the €50m valuation plus bonuses that could have weighed heavily on his shoulders, Diego hasn’t taken long to win over Milan fans. In his last six league matches (he missed two due to injury), he’s scored four goals and provided three assists.

He has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

Industry observers note that moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. Diego is succeeding remarkably, as his assist for Christian Pulisic in the derby shows, as he got past Carlo Augusto and crossed.

Moreira made the difference against Italy on Sunday too: not only did he score the fourth goal, which he celebrated by making a gesture of ‘one, two, three and four’ with his fingers, but he also kept accelerating, hit the woodwork, shot wide once more and had two shots blocked by his opponents.

It has been revealed that he set up De Bruyne for a shot, had more touches than anyone else in the opponents’ area (11) and often took on Calafiori and Dimarco, delighting the crowd with a spectacular backheel. He had around 50 touches and 27/31 completed passes, earning the applause of the entire stadium when he came off.

According to recent reports, moreira is currently captivating thanks to his drive and desire. He’s that way at Milan and he’s that way with the national team. That’s why there’s a version of the Rossoneri with him and another without him which, frankly, isn’t as threatening.

Amorim carefully integrated him into the team’s operations at the start of the season, but now he has broken the padlock off and now considers him a key player in the team. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

Recent findings suggest that with four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

Sources indicate that the leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

#3120. All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 29m • 📚 Deep Dive (5899 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 newly introduced players, but did not upgrade two of the most important positions on the pitch.

Sources indicate that only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the big difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

According to recent reports, zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, launched a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

In a recent development, suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a significant mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

Sources indicate that “We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

Recent findings suggest that that sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he said: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

It has been revealed that it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Industry observers note that jackson was not the only Villa latest boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Industry observers note that johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

Industry observers note that “They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery said. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

According to recent reports, “Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig.

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:.

vs Man Utd (A) - Oct 10th, 5.30pm.

vs Coventry (H) - Oct 19th, 8pm.

vs Chelsea (A) - Oct 24th, 5.30pm.

vs Crystal Palace (H) - Oct 31st, 5.30pm.

vs Brentford (H) - Oct 10th, 3pm.

vs Fenerbahce (H) - Oct 14th, 8pm.

vs Newcastle (A) - Oct 17th, 5.30pm.

Good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side right now sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

According to recent reports, tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

But before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 12:39, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 12:46.

Returning to Scottish Premiership action for the first time in two weeks, Motherwell welcome an in-form Rangers side to Fir Park on Saturday afternoon.

The Well head into the fixture following a 1-1 draw away to Dundee United, while the Gers extended their unbeaten run in all competitions to 12 matches with a 2-0 victory over St Mirren, leaving them four points behind league leaders Celtic with a game in hand.

After an impressive fourth-placed finish in the Scottish Premiership last season under Jens Berthel Askou, Motherwell secured European football and earned widespread praise for their attacking style of play.

However, Askou left Fir Park over the summer to take charge of Toulouse, with the North Lanarkshire club appointing Swedish coach Alfred Johansson as his replacement, although he has so far struggled to build on the progress made during the 2025-26 campaign.

After 13 Scottish Premiership matches, the Well sit ninth in the table with three wins, four draws and six defeats, having conceded 21 goals, with only three sides shipping more, while just three teams have scored fewer than their 14.

Despite their worrying start to the new season, Motherwell entered the final international break of the year on the back of a three-match unbeaten run, with draws against St Johnstone and Dundee United either side of a narrow 1-0 victory over St Mirren on Halloween.

While that positive end to October and start to November has offered some encouragement to Johansson's side, they will know they must pick up where they left off before the two-week break to create more breathing room above the bottom two and close the gap on the teams higher up the table.

As for Rangers, they appear to have put their difficult start under Derek McInnes behind them, with the Gers heading into the busy festive period in a strong position to challenge for silverware and close in on rivals Celtic in the Premiership title race.

McInnes's side entered the break with a 2-0 away victory over St Mirren, courtesy of goals either side of half-time from Ryan Naderi and Dan Neil, extending their unbeaten run to 12 matches and marking their first defeat-free spell since August, which has also included two victories over their bitter Glasgow rivals.

This impressive turnaround has followed an early European exit and a difficult start to their domestic campaign under the former Hearts boss, but Rangers are now showing significant signs of improvement compared to recent seasons.

At this stage last year, the Gers were fourth in the table and had recently replaced Russell Martin with Danny Rohl, following another difficult managerial spell, while they had also been sitting third 12 months earlier, highlighting the progress McInnes has made since taking charge.

Despite their recent resurgence, Rangers remain four points behind Celtic, although a victory on Saturday would cut that gap to a single point, with a game in hand on the league leaders still to come.

The sides meet for the second time this season following Rangers' narrow 1-0 victory at Ibrox in early September, with the Gers having since turned their home ground into something of a fortress, as no side has taken a point off them there since their defeat on matchweek two.

Motherwell Scottish Premiership form:.

Rangers Scottish Premiership form:.

Rangers form (all competitions):.

Motherwell could name the same starting XI that drew 1-1 with Dundee United, although they remain without several first-team players through injury.

Alex Lowry, Johnny Koutroumbis and Dylan Williams are all expected to miss out due to knee, muscle and hamstring problems respectively, although the trio could return by the start of December.

Lukas Fadinger has scored twice in his last two appearances, albeit both goals coming from the penalty spot, and is expected to anchor the midfield while wearing the captain's armband once again.

Meanwhile, the visitors make the short journey south with a longer list of injury concerns, although they at least avoided any fresh setbacks during their victory over St Mirren.

McInnes will remain without Ross McCrorie, Cameron Devlin, Daisuke Yokota, Lawrence Shankland, Youssef Chermiti and Jose Cifuentes, although Chermiti is the only one of the injured players expected to remain sidelined into 2027.

Motherwell possible starting lineup:.

Paulsen; Sparrow, Girdwood-Reich, Moormann, Longelo; Hodge, Fadinger; Maswanhise, Remarked, Kanga; Palmer-Houlden.

Rangers possible starting lineup:.

Pandur; Sterling, Makhanya, Fernandez, Penrice; Bouanni, Neil, Raskin, Kim Min-Su; Naderi, Kelsy.

Motherwell head into the fixture with some encouraging momentum after going three matches unbeaten, but we expect their progress to be halted by an in-form Rangers side, who should secure their ninth league victory of the season and further close the gap on Celtic.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sheffield United face Watford in their first match after the international break on Saturday.
  • The scoreline wasn’t the only dampener on a tough day in South London, as Femi Seriki was stretchered off.
  • In a recent development, in better news, top scorer Patrick Bamford is fit to return against the Hornets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sheffield United face Watford in their first match after the international break on Saturday. SUFC will be eager to return to form, having seen a four-game unbeaten run ended by a 2-1 loss at Charlton Athletic in their last outing.

The scoreline wasn’t the only dampener on a tough day in South London, as Femi Seriki was stretchered off. Blades boss Chris Wilder swiftly confirmed he had ruptured his patella tendon, and speaking to BBC Sheffield’s Andy Giddings ahead of the Watford game, he has now said that Seriki faces 12 months on the sidelines after undergoing surgery.

In a recent development, in better news, top scorer Patrick Bamford is fit to return against the Hornets. Those still on the sidelines include Ryan One, Matt Doherty and Jamie Shackleton.

The Seriki upgrade is one that Sheffield United fans saw coming. There was immediate concern when he went down against the Addicks, and Wilder’s confirmation that he had ruptured his patella tendon meant that his recovery timescale was never going to be short.

It means the Blades will almost certainly continue with Hamza Choudhury at right-back, especially with Doherty and Shackleton still out as well.

Bamford’s return doesn’t help the right-back problems, but it is a welcome boost for SUFC nonetheless. With five Championship goals, he is their top scorer in the league this season.

The experienced frontman offers a level of finishing that none of his fellow strikers can. Of the forwards available to Wilder, he is also the best at using his body to hold up the ball and bring fellow attackers into the game, so his comeback increases the threat level of the entire frontline.

Sheffield United’s strikers are often a point of frustration. Bamford has proven to be a fine addition since joining on a free transfer last season, notching 19 goals and two assists in all competitions.

However, Tom Cannon still hasn’t come good on his £10m fee, Tyrese Campbell hasn’t hit the heights of his debut campaign at SUFC, and Ben Brereton Diaz has had a limited impact since his return in the summer.

It has been revealed that jordan Ayew scored in the Charlton Athletic loss and will hope to build on that, but he isn’t a long-term option at 35. Sidelined striker One has shown promise, but he is one for the future at only 20.

Bamford is the clear standout at striker, and his comeback from injury is a very welcome one.

AC Milan have the financial capability to go out and sign their top targets in January, according to Gianluca Di Marzio.
